steps.what: Identify site journeys and performance questions that matter
Define measures, populations, units and collection conditions
Configure collection queries and metric expressions
Test metrics against known sessions and collection failures
Approve the final metric configuration and collection scope
Activate the approved metric configuration

tasks.design: Use the existing web-observability category of {OTHER} and {BI} metric builders before writing custom collectors. Reusable expressions and collection profiles reduce configuration work; the administrator defines the measures, tests known sessions and approves the exact configuration before activation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each metric can be configured from scratch despite similar collection patterns.
tasks.enabler_now: Native metric builders can reuse validated expressions and collection profiles.
tasks.still_hard: A technically correct metric can measure the wrong journey or miss slow clients.
tasks.human_edge: Choose meaningful measures and recognise sampling bias.

ambition.what: Compare release performance for a named critical checkout or enquiry journey.

tasks.altitude: Less repetitive configuration; the administrator still negotiates what good performance means.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-10 for telemetry access and applicable national consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: metric builders can reuse collection profiles and expressions; measurement definitions and validation remain human.

assumptions: Boundary: developing and activating metrics, not ongoing monitoring or the site's existing telemetry runtime. Shares are provisional work estimates, not prior buckets.

Existing instrumentation supplies timestamp, route, duration, status, release_id and sampling flags in a documented telemetry schema. s2 supplies metric_name, formula, unit, population and collection_conditions; s4 creates known sessions and counts their manual execution. Missing telemetry requires manual investigation, with no promised collector coverage.

Native metric builders are tested first. s3 savings are fewer repeated expression/configuration edits, not reduced metric definition or validation. Activation s6 is near-zero at schema minimum 1%, fully retained.
Gross 12%; focal upkeep 1.5 gives net 10.5%. Any mapping maintenance is human upkeep, never system runtime.
unknowns: Current observability features and telemetry gaps
Whether profile reuse actually replaces repeated edits
research_questions: Do configured metrics match known sessions including failed and missing events?

already_counted.description: Approve tested metric scope and meaning

incremental.description: Revalidate profiles after telemetry schema changes

approvals.approved_version: approved metric configuration v1 final expressions, scope and collection settings; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 0% if native profiles already cover the work with no change; 8% if schema gaps retain 2.5 extra baseline hours versus central net 10.5%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate with developers on websites and web projects.

steps.what: Review the requested site change and delivery constraints
Agree scope, dependencies and responsibilities with developers
Write project tasks and acceptance points from the agreement
Review work with developers and resolve delivery issues
Complete and verify final task decisions and handover details
Save the approved project update

tasks.design: Configure task templates in {PROJECT} for recurring site-change and campaign work, with standard dependency and acceptance headings. The administrator writes the particular scope and resolves issues with developers; no model runs the project or releases a site.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated project scaffolding is rewritten for similar changes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing project templates can supply standard fields while leaving decisions explicit.
tasks.still_hard: Trade-offs across content, technical dependencies and launch commitments.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate achievable scope and resolve disagreements.
tasks.altitude: A small task-writing saving; delivery and release rights are unchanged.

reach.task: Maintain a clear dependency and acceptance record

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-5 for board access and applicable national consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: project templates reduce repeated task scaffolding without making scope decisions.

assumptions: Boundary: focal administrator collaboration and project records. Developer implementation and progress reporting are unchanged outside the focal denominator; there is no transfer or automated deployment.

s2 supplies actual scope, dependencies and responsibilities. s3 captures task_text, owner, dependency and acceptance_point manually; the template supplies headings only. Developers supply their existing progress report before s4. Missing facts are resolved in discussion, not generated.
Test native task templates first. Only repeated scaffolding in s3 loses time. s6 is a near-zero native save with minimum 1% fully retained.
Gross 3%; focal template upkeep 0.4 gives net 2.6%.
research_questions: Do templates help without creating irrelevant tasks?

already_counted.description: Verify final project decisions and handover

approvals.approved_version: approved project update v1 final scope, tasks and decisions; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 0% when templates already exist and no change is deployed; 2% if upkeep takes one rather than central 0.4 hours per 100 baseline hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Inventory connected services and read interface specifications
Determine semantic, authentication and version compatibility requirements
Exercise interfaces with representative valid and invalid test messages
Write requirements and remedies supported by the test results
Check and approve the final interoperability requirements
Save the approved interface requirements

tasks.design: Try the existing API-test category of {OTHER} first, then build a deterministic runner only for repeated contract tests it cannot perform. The administrator selects fixtures, reviews failures and records requirements in {DOCS}; software checks syntax and declared contracts, not business meaning.
tasks.previous_blocker: Representative contract messages are repeatedly executed and compared by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable fixture-based checks can exercise exact schemas and error responses.
tasks.still_hard: Matching field names does not establish matching business meaning or acceptable failure handling.
tasks.human_edge: Identify semantic and operational dependencies beyond the published schema.

ambition.what: Recheck contract compatibility for every interface-version proposal.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated test execution; requirements remain an accountable technical judgement.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-8 for non-production credentials and applicable national consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: deterministic contract tests can replay fixtures and compare declared response contracts.

assumptions: Boundary is identifying requirements through tests and recording remedies, not deploying interface changes. Existing automated test runtime is excluded; savings require actual repeated manual execution today.

Interface owners supply endpoint, method, schema_version, authentication_scheme, status_contract and field definitions. The administrator selects and prepares fixtures in s3; fixture preparation, safe credentials and result interpretation are included in its retained 50%. Missing specs or fixtures retain manual investigation.
Test native contract-test settings first. Run only in a non-production environment with synthetic fixtures; no production write or external business message is performed by this design.
s6 is a near-zero native save at minimum 1% fully retained. Gross 10%; focal harness upkeep 0.8 gives net 9.2%.
research_questions: Do tests exercise failures and version transitions as well as valid payloads?

already_counted.description: Prepare fixtures and interpret contract-test results

approvals.approved_version: approved interface requirements v1 final compatibility findings and remedies; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 0% when repeated checks are already automated and no change is deployed; 7% if new fixture preparation costs 2.2 more baseline hours than central net 9.2%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop and implement ongoing website revision procedures.

steps.what: Examine the current revision process and recent change failures
Choose revision roles, checks, rollback and approval conditions
Write the procedure and configure its revision checklist draft

loop.input: Administrator-selected roles, actual revision actions, checks, rollback triggers and approval rules
loop.output: Procedure draft and matching checklist text
loop.check: s4 rehearses actual steps; s5 verifies every action and gate matches selected controls and tested results
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unsupported instructions return to manual authoring
loop.why_not_simpler: Use a native checklist template for fixed steps; a language draft helps explain site-specific exception and rollback conditions in a coherent procedure.

steps.what: Rehearse revisions and rollback and correct the draft procedure
Approve the tested final procedure and checklist
Publish the approved internal procedure and checklist

tasks.design: Start with native checklist configuration in {PROJECT} and procedure templates in {DOCS}. A bounded loop may draft explanatory text from administrator-selected controls; the administrator rehearses revisions and rollback on a test site in {CMS}, corrects the draft and approves the final procedure before internal publication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site-specific controls must be translated into clear operational instructions.
tasks.enabler_now: Controlled drafting can reduce prose assembly while native templates hold recurring checks.
tasks.still_hard: A convincing procedure can still fail under real permissions and rollback constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Choose acceptable change risk and prove that rollback is practical.

ambition.what: Provide a rehearsed rollback checklist for routine content revisions.

tasks.altitude: Less prose assembly; control selection and rehearsal remain central to the week.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-10 for test access and applicable national consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: bounded drafting can help document selected operational controls; testing and accountable approval remain necessary.

assumptions: Boundary: develop, rehearse and activate a revision procedure, not perform every later website change. Production releases and existing pipeline runtime earn no saving here.

s1 identifies actual revision actions and failures; s2 records actor, ordered_action, prerequisite, check, rollback_trigger and approver. Missing action details are captured manually before drafting, not inferred. s4 produces the final corrected procedure after rehearsal.
Test native templates/checklists first. The loop drafts text only and cannot change the site. s6 is near-zero native publication represented by minimum 1% fully retained.
Gross saving 12%; focal procedure upkeep 1.2 gives central net 10.8%.
unknowns: Actual revision controls and delegated approval rights
research_questions: Can a new administrator execute the tested procedure without guessing?

already_counted.description: Review draft wording while assembling the procedure

incremental.description: Audit generated wording and maintain drafting constraints

approvals.approved_version: approved revision procedure v1 final tested text and checklist; changed instructions require renewed approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 0% where a native template already suffices and no drafting tool is deployed; 8% if corrections require 2.8 extra baseline hours beyond central net 10.8%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repetitive configuration, test execution and procedure prose while retaining metric, interface and release-control judgement.
role.ambitious_version: A web administrator who can show whether the site works, explain its interface requirements and maintain rehearsed revision controls.
